name: IMA homepage: the Institute of Management Accountants member landing page
title: IMA homepage: the Institute of Management Accountants member landing page
answer: This is the homepage of the Institute of Management Accountants, a global association for accounting and finance professionals with more than 140,000 members. It is a membership and marketing page rather than a research document. The most useful thing it states is that IMA describes itself as sitting at the intersection of accounting, finance and business strategy, and that its research-backed Competency Framework defines 10 core skill areas for modern accounting and finance professionals. It does not mention artificial intelligence anywhere.

sections.body: This is the homepage of the Institute of Management Accountants, published by IMA itself. It is a promotional and membership page rather than a research report, a standards document or a dated article. Its scope is the association's offer to accounting and finance professionals: certifications, continuing professional education, networking, local chapters, conferences and career resources. No publication date is stated on the page. The text was harvested on 28 September 2026. The page describes IMA as a worldwide association for accounting and finance professionals and invites readers to join more than 140,000 members.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page introduces the Institute of Management Accountants as a global association at the intersection of accounting, finance and business strategy, saying it provides knowledge and connections that help teams and individuals feel impactful, confident and successful. Much of the text promotes credentials. It states that earning a credential from IMA signals more than technical skill, showing an employer that the holder thinks strategically, makes sound decisions and understands the bigger business picture. The CMA, or Certified Management Accountant, is described as the globally recognized standard in management accounting and a proven path to bigger roles and better opportunities, with credentials offered for every career stage. The page also points to a research-backed Competency Framework that defines 10 core skill areas modern accounting and finance professionals need, with an invitation to assess gaps and then choose training and learning pathways that fit a role and goals. It advertises hands-on learning through global conferences, workshops and live webinars, and local chapters for in-person networking. One member testimonial describes IMA as a professional family that helped the person develop as a leader. The page closes by saying its courses and certifications help members stay ahead with the latest trends, research and best practices in management accounting.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The page gives a membership figure of more than 140,000 members. It states that the IMA Competency Framework defines 10 core skill areas for modern accounting and finance professionals. It claims the CMA is the globally recognized standard in management accounting. It also claims that an IMA credential signals strategic thinking, sound decision making and understanding of the bigger business picture. The text gives no figures or claims about artificial intelligence.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in accounting would use this page only as background on the body that serves management accountants and the controller's office, not as a source on AI itself. The page names the CMA credential and a Competency Framework of 10 skill areas, which shows where IMA defines the skills it expects of finance professionals, and that is the natural place to look for later AI-related competency work. The page does not support the claim that IMA publishes research on AI implementation inside corporate finance and CFO organizations, because it contains no mention of AI, no research publications and no implementation guidance.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Accounting

sections.body: This is a commercial landing page for a professional association, written to recruit members and sell certifications, so it is promotional in tone and gives no independent evidence. It is undated. It does not cover artificial intelligence, AI adoption, tools, vendors, controls or implementation practice in any form. It lists no research reports, no authors and no findings, and it offers no data on how finance teams use technology. Anyone citing it for AI in accounting would be citing a page that says nothing about AI.
